questions.q: How does deception technology relate to a honeypot?
options: They are two unrelated and competing security approaches
Deception technology only refers to decoys used on web applications
A honeypot is a newer replacement for deception technology
A honeypot is one decoy system; deception technology is the broader category of fake assets planted throughout an environment
questions.explain: A honeypot is one implementation of the broader deception technology category, which also includes honeytokens, decoy shares, and fake AD objects.

options: A dedicated decoy server running a full operating system
A real credential that is rotated automatically every 24 hours
A fake credential, file, or database entry planted to trigger an alert if accessed or used
A type of encryption key used to protect honeypot traffic
questions.explain: Unlike a honeypot, a honeytoken isn't a system at all — it's a single piece of bait planted inside a real environment.

questions.q: Why does a fake AWS access key sitting in a config file work as an effective honeytoken?
options: Because it automatically grants real cloud access to anyone who finds it
Because no legitimate process should ever use it, so its use is unambiguous evidence of compromise
Because it slows down any attacker who tries to read the file
Because AWS requires every account to maintain at least one fake key
questions.explain: Since the key has no legitimate purpose, any attempt to use it is a reliable, unambiguous signal of unauthorized activity.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a fake Active Directory object, such as a decoy admin account?
options: To catch an attacker performing directory reconnaissance to plan privilege escalation
To give real administrators a backup account in case their primary one is locked
To automatically disable all other accounts in the same group
To replace the need for multi-factor authentication on real admin accounts
questions.explain: No legitimate administrator would ever authenticate as or query a decoy account or fake group, making interaction with it a tripwire.

questions.q: Why does spreading deception widely across an environment catch more lateral movement than relying on a single honeypot?
options: It reduces the total number of decoys an organization needs to maintain
It guarantees an attacker will never successfully breach the network
It multiplies the number of tripwires an attacker might trip, without needing a dedicated decoy system for each one
It eliminates the need for any logging or alerting infrastructure
questions.explain: Honeytokens, decoy shares, and fake AD objects can be planted cheaply almost anywhere, giving far more chances to catch an attacker than one honeypot.
